title: A deterministic CTE read twice is inlined and computed per reference
verdict: inlined: one aggregate and one scan per reference; a non-deterministic CTE is kept once
description: WITH c AS (SELECT k, sum(x) AS v FROM t GROUP BY k) SELECT ... FROM c a JOIN c b ON a.k = b.k has two HashAggregate(sum) nodes in the executed plan, each over its own scan of t: the CTE is inlined and the sum computed per reference, in an order the partitioning sets per scan (spark-sum-double).

A CTE with rand() is not inlined: joined with itself, no row's two reads differ (three runs). SUM counts as deterministic, so a double SUM's CTE is inlined. A check root and a sink root over one CTE may read two evaluations of the sum, which a margin of 2ε covers; whether the two scans of a table read one version (a Delta or Iceberg source) is not characterized.
reference: The reference evaluates a shared subplan once (Rel.eval).

evidence.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT k, sum(x) AS v FROM t GROUP BY k) SELECT a.k, a.v, b.v FROM c a JOIN c b ON a.k = b.k
evidence.observed: executedPlan: two HashAggregate(keys=[k], functions=[sum(x)]), each over Exchange and its own Scan ExistingRDD

evidence.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT id, rand() AS r FROM t) SELECT count(*) FROM c a JOIN c b ON a.id = b.id WHERE a.r <> b.r
